definitions.gloss: miso-pickled food, food preserved in miso paste
definitions.explanation: Vegetables, fish, or meat that have been pickled or marinated in miso paste, both as a preservation method and for flavor.

examples.japanese: {大根|だいこん}の{味噌漬|みそづ}けを{作|つく}った。
{味噌漬|みそづ}けの{魚|さかな}は{焼|や}くと{香|こう}ばしい。
examples.english: Miso-pickled fish smells wonderful when grilled.

examples.japanese: おばあちゃんの{味噌漬|みそづ}けは{何日|なんにち}も{漬|つ}け{込|こ}んであるので{味|あじ}が{深|ふか}い。
examples.english: Grandma's miso pickles have a deep flavor because they've been pickling for many days.

notes:
A traditional Japanese preservation and cooking method where food is packed in miso paste. The miso both flavors and preserves the food. Common items include vegetables ({野菜|やさい}), fish ({魚|さかな}), and tofu.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {味噌漬|みそづ}けの{野菜|やさい}: miso-pickled vegetables
- {味噌漬|みそづ}けにする: to pickle in miso
- {西京|さいきょう}{味噌漬|みそづ}け: Saikyo miso marinade (sweet white miso, popular for fish)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {塩漬|しおづ}け: salt-pickled (preserved in salt)
- {粕漬|かすづ}け: sake lees pickle (preserved in sake lees)
- {漬物|つけもの}: pickles (general term for Japanese pickled foods)
